messages:
IncidentBot: Paging @Ava (oncall) for GPU stability alert on cluster-gamma (xid errors + ECC warnings).
Ava (oncall): saw the alert, looking now. which nodes?
Ravi (infra): it's nodes g-gamma-[03,07,11] showing repeated Xid 43/45 resets and ECC corrected error spikes. telemetry shows heartbeat drops before resets.
Jonas (serving): we started getting container restarts on those nodes ~2m ago, about ~120 failed inference requests/min for model 'small-llm-v2'.
Marta (CS): any customer impact visible? CS dashboards show increased 5xx on a handful of enterprise tenants in us-east-1, one support ticket opened.
Priya (SRE): looking at dmesg from g-gamma-03, seeing nvme + nvidia messages: "NVRM: Xid (43): GPU has fallen off the bus." also lots of ECC corrected: "EDAC MC: ECC error, CPU recovered"
Ava (oncall): ok, immediate plan: cordon g-gamma-03 and 07, drain in-flight jobs, failover routing for requests currently targeting those nodes. Can infra run a live-driver-restart on 11 only if it's safe?
Ravi (infra): we can attempt nvidia-driver reload on 11 but 03 and 07 already have container crashes; prefer to evacuate. I'll start cordon/drain.
Jonas (serving): enabling model fallback policy now: route new requests to 'small-llm-v2-quant' replicas in us-east-2. Will also enable degraded-caching to reduce KV pressure.
Marta (CS): notified affected customers with a short update: "We're seeing GPU instability in us-east-1, routing to healthy capacity. We'll post updates in 15 mins."
Ava (oncall): runbook step: collect /var/log/messages, nvidia-smi -q, and kernel logs. Priya, can you pull heap profiles from containers before they restart?
Priya (SRE): grabbing logs now. Attaching current nvidia-smi snapshot: 
```
Timestamp: 2026-03-15T14:21:03Z
GPU 0: Temp 78C, ECC (Volatile) corrected=1123, Xid Count=5
Processes: inference-server (pid 4211) - crashed 2x
```
Ava (oncall): thanks. Ravi, what's the state of PCIe firmware and recent driver rollouts? Any recent kernel or driver bumps?
Ravi (infra): no driver rollouts in last 24h. Kernel patch applied to a subset two days ago on g-gamma-11, but 03/07 didn't get it. Strange that 11 is showing some telemetry heartbeat suppression but hasn't OOMed.
Jonas (serving): we see a pattern: long-running KV cache lookups lead to increasing resident set until container gets SIGKILL during driver reset. Could be memory leak + driver instability combo.
Priya (SRE): searching crash logs: container crashed shortly after Xid 45, and kernel logged: "nvhost: gpu reset required". Crash loop started ~T-3m.
Ava (oncall): mitigation checklist executed: cordon/drain on 03,07; driver-reload attempt on 11 blocked by system caution. Start node reboot on 03 after drain. On 07, keep pods in evicted state for now.
Ravi (infra): initiating reboot of g-gamma-03 (graceful). Also flagging these hosts for hardware ECC validation tomorrow.
Marta (CS): updating customers: "We've routed traffic away from affected capacity and restarted impacted tasks. You may see transient errors for up to 10 minutes — full recovery estimate 20m."
Jonas (serving): scaling up additional replicas in us-east-2 and us-west-1 to absorb throughput. Also flipping aggressive retry window from 2s to 6s to avoid immediate failover storms.
Priya (SRE): post-drain telemetry: error rate for 'small-llm-v2' is trending down from 8% to 1.8% after routing changes. CPU/memory on fallback nodes stable.
Ava (oncall): good. next: collect hardware telemetry and snapshot GPU ECC counters across the cluster. Also, capture PCIe link state for g-gamma hosts. Ravi please schedule an overnight maintenance for deeper hardware loop.
Ravi (infra): will open maintenance ticket and reserve onsite tech for ECC diagnostics. Also tagging bios/PCH firmware to be validated.
Jonas (serving): separate note: recommend adding short-circuit fallback earlier in routing policy when Xid spikes detected — reduce wasted tokens. I'll open a rollout PR for policy + metric alert.
Marta (CS): CS on standby for customers that ask for incident timelines — please ping when we have ETA for full node return.
Priya (SRE): logs and traces uploaded to incident bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/2391234567/logs.tar.gz. Collected kernel oops, docker logs, and nvidia-smi snapshots.
Ava (oncall): linking runbook entry here for postmortem: https://confluence/redwood/runbooks/gpu-driver-reset. We'll do an initial blameless postmortem after stable for 48h.
IncidentBot: Incident 2391234567 status changed to INVESTIGATING -> MITIGATED (partial).
Ava (oncall): final quick notes: cause hypothesis = combination of ECC-corrected spike + transient PCIe heartbeat suppression triggering driver resets under memory pressure. Impact = transient 5xx spikes for select customers in us-east-1, mitigated by routing and node reboots. Follow-ups: hardware checks, routing policy change, better preemptive eviction on Xid surge.
Marta (CS): thanks all, I'll send a summary to affected customers and our CS leads. :thumbsup:
Ravi (infra): leaving nodes cordoned until after hardware validation. Will post when they're ready to rejoin.
Jonas (serving): tracking follow-up PRs in #eng-runtime, will reference incident id 2391234567.
Ava (oncall): handing off to Priya for overnight watch. Priya, you're the lead until 0800 PST.
Priya (SRE): acknowledged — will escalate if any recurrence.
_note: No title field per agents.md; messages concatenated into one continuous string with sender prefixes.
